notes.claim: The 4 to 20 mA loop is a 0 to 100 percent scale, and its straight-line conversion is y = mx + b.
A 12 mA signal from a differential-pressure cell is 50% pressure difference but 71% flow rate.

sources.title: Relating 4 to 20 mA Signals to Instrument Variables | Understanding Analog Instrumentation | Textbook
sources.quote: Each real-world value must be converted into its analog current equivalent, then into a scaled integer value, and finally back into a real-world representation, all with the linear equation: y=mx+b.

sources.title: Square root scaling for differential pressure flowmeters - Control Engineering
sources.quote: But the root of a number from 0-1 is larger: √0.5 = 0.707. So if there is a 12 mA signal from the DP cell, that’s 50% DP, but 71% flow rate.
